newsitem.title: USA: British nanny indicted for first degree murder.
newsitem.headline: British nanny indicted for first degree murder.

text.p: A grand jury indicted an 18-year-old British nanny on a first-degree murder charge on Wednesday in the death of a 9-month-old boy in her care.

Officials said the Middlesex County grand jury alleged that Louise Woodward of Chester, England, caused Matthew Eappen's death last month by severely shaking him and striking his head on a hard surface, causing a skull fracture.

Woodward, who came to the United States in June 1996 to work as an au pair, has already pleaded not guilty to a charge of assault and battery in Eappen's death. She will enter a plea on the first degree murder charge in a Cambridge, Massachusetts, court on Friday, the county district attorney's office said.

Woodward is being held without bail at a Massachusetts prison in Framingham outside Boston. If convicted of first-degree murder she would face a mandatory sentence of life in prison with no eligibility for parole, the district attorney's office said.

Woodward's lawyer said the grand jury did not get a chance to hear some evidence in her support because the county declined to postpone the indictment process. "A slower, more deliberative, and ultimately fairer investigation would not have resulted in this indictment," lawyer Andrew Good said in a statement.

Woodward called rescue workers to her employer's home in upscale Newton, Massachusetts, on Feb. 5 and told them the boy had suddenly stopped breathing after being sick all day. He was diagnosed with head trauma consistent with shaken-baby syndrome.
He was on life support for four days before he died of a brain haemorrhage on Feb. 9. Autopsy reports ruled the cause of death was a blunt blow to the head.
Woodward had lived with and cared for Matthew Eappen and his 2-year old brother, whose parents are both doctors at Children's Hospital in Boston, beginning in November.
